senses.gloss: ऋभु॑ mfn. (√ रभ्), clever, skilful, inventive, prudent (said of Indra, Agni, and the Ādityas, RV.; also of property or wealth, RV. iv, 37, 5; viii, 93, 34; of an arrow, AV. i, 2, 3)
they appear generally as accompanying Indra, especially at the evening sacrifice
in later mythology Ṛbhu is a son of Brahman, VP.
ऋभु॑ (अवस्), m. a class of deities
ऋभु [cf. Gk. ἀλϕεῖν; Lat. labor; Goth. arb-aiths; Angl.Sax. earfoð; Slav. rab-ǔ.]
ऋभु—म॑त् mfn. clever, skilful, prudent, RV. i, 111, 2
accompanied by or connected with the Ṛbhus, RV.; VS. xxxviii, 8; AitBr. ii, 20, 14; KātyŚr.
ऋभु—ष्ठिर (voc.) mfn. clever and wise (said of Indra), RV. viii, 77, 8.
(this word appears to owe its origin to the next.)
ऋभुक्षि॑न् आस्, m. (see Gr. 162 Pāṇ. vii, 1, 85 ff.), N. of the above Ṛbhus, and esp. of the first of them, RV.
N. of Indra (as the lord of the Ṛbhus, Nir.), RV.
ऋभुक्षीण Nom. P. ऋभुक्षीणति, to behave like Ṛbhukṣin, Siddh.
